sections.name: Technical Writing & Documentation
sections.outcome: Create accurate, usable, maintainable technical documentation by planning for readers, selecting an appropriate document form, organizing verified content, and satisfying delivery constraints.
includes: Tutorials, how-to guides, explanations, and troubleshooting guides
Technical specifications, requirements, design proposals, and decision records
excludes: Creative writing whose purpose is not technical communication
Domain problem solving without a documentation deliverable
Unsupported claims presented as established facts

sample_tasks.instruction: Given a short fact sheet and a named reader, write one accurate paragraph that explains what the described tool does and why that reader would use it.

Given verified facts, interface definitions, user goals, design alternatives, delivery rules, and a product change, produce a coherent documentation set containing an audience and content plan, reference material, an instructional guide, a design record, and a reviewed maintenance update.

sections.name: Documentation Planning
sections.outcome: Plan documentation around defined readers and tasks, verified content, and a navigable information structure.
includes: Selection of document types for user needs
excludes: Drafting complete reference, instructional, or design documents
Visual branding and promotional positioning
Project plans unrelated to documentation content

sample_tasks.instruction: Given a product description and two possible readers, identify the primary reader and the single task the document should help that reader complete.

Given notes for a new developer tool, produce a documentation plan that defines reader groups and tasks, separates verified facts from unresolved claims, and organizes the needed pages into a navigable content structure.

sections.name: Audience and Task Analysis
sections.outcome: Translate reader roles, prior knowledge, constraints, and goals into concrete documentation requirements.
includes: Information needed before, during, and after a task
excludes: Writing the final procedure or reference page
Market segmentation based only on purchasing behavior
Inventing reader needs unsupported by the brief

sample_tasks.instruction: Given one reader role and one product goal, state the reader's likely starting knowledge and immediate information need.
Analyze a mixed audience of operators, integrators, and maintainers, then define each group's goals, assumptions, risks, and required documentation without duplicating material unnecessarily.

sections.name: Content Evidence and Claim Control
sections.outcome: Distinguish established facts, permitted inferences, choices, and unknowns so technical claims remain accurate and traceable.
excludes: Independent factual research not requested by the task
Schema validation as the primary operation
Copyediting claims without checking their support

sample_tasks.instruction: Classify each statement in a short technical brief as stated fact, reasonable inference, author choice, or unresolved question.

From a set of partially conflicting engineering notes, build a claim inventory that preserves supported facts, marks assumptions, identifies contradictions, and lists the questions that must be resolved before publication.

sections.name: Information Architecture
sections.outcome: Organize technical content into discoverable document units whose sequence and hierarchy match reader tasks.
excludes: Sentence-level prose revision
Interface design outside the documentation system
Arbitrary organization by the order in which notes were received

sample_tasks.instruction: For a defined reader task, arrange five supplied facts under a small heading hierarchy in the order the reader will need them.
Using defined reader goals and prior knowledge, design the page structure, navigation, and cross-references for documentation that serves first-time setup, routine operation, and occasional lookup.

sections.name: API and Reference Documentation
sections.outcome: Produce precise, consistently structured lookup documentation for interfaces, data models, products, and schema-constrained technical records.
excludes: Learning-oriented walkthroughs
Diagnostic narratives organized around symptoms
Design arguments and option selection

sample_tasks.instruction: Using an existing audience, evidence, and structure plan, write one concise reference entry for a configuration field with its type, allowed values, default behavior, and effect.

For a networked monitoring device, create an integrated reference package that documents one API operation, its request and response models, the device's technical specifications, and a schema-conformant configuration record derived from the supplied facts.

sections.name: API Operation Reference
sections.outcome: Document callable operations so readers can identify purpose, invocation requirements, behavior, results, errors, and constraints without reconstructing them from implementation details.
excludes: Full data-model catalogs
Step-by-step application tutorials
Implementation internals that do not affect callers

sample_tasks.instruction: From a verified interface definition, document one operation's purpose, required input, and returned result for the planned reader.

Write a complete reference entry for an asynchronous operation, including invocation form, parameters, authentication conditions, side effects, response behavior, failure cases, limits, and a minimal usage example.

sections.name: Data Model Reference
sections.outcome: Document structured data contracts with unambiguous field semantics, constraints, nesting, allowed values, and relationships.
excludes: Producing a particular data instance as the main deliverable
Database design rationale
API operation sequencing

sample_tasks.instruction: Document one field from a supplied model by stating its meaning, type, required status, and allowed range.

Produce a structured reference for a nested event model, covering every field, required and optional status, types, formats, enumerations, cross-field constraints, and the representation of invalid or unavailable values.

sections.name: Product Specifications
sections.outcome: Turn verified product facts into a complete, consistently organized technical specification that supports comparison and implementation decisions.
includes: Capacities, dimensions, compatibility, and environmental limits
excludes: Promotional feature claims
Requirements for a product that has not yet been designed
Narrative setup instructions

sample_tasks.instruction: Convert a small set of verified device facts into a labeled specification block with normalized units.

Write a comprehensive technical specification for a portable computing device, organizing verified facts across processing, display, cameras, sensors, connectivity, power, ports, environmental limits, and supported media while clearly marking unavailable values.

sections.name: Schema-Constrained Technical Records
sections.outcome: Map technical facts into syntactically valid structured documents that satisfy required fields, types, formats, enumerations, nesting, and additional-property rules.
includes: Required properties, formats, enums, ranges, and property closure
excludes: Designing a new schema
Claiming chosen values were present in the input
Prose documentation when no structured record is required

sample_tasks.instruction: Given a flat schema with three required fields and a short factual description, produce one valid structured record and choose a permitted value only where the description is silent.

Transform a narrative operational plan into a nested JSON record under a supplied schema, preserving supported facts, making only permitted choices for missing values, and satisfying every required property, type, date format, range, enumeration, and no-extra-properties constraint.

sections.name: Instructional and Support Documentation
sections.outcome: Create task-oriented and learning-oriented documentation that helps readers understand a system, complete goals, and recover from problems.
excludes: Lookup-only reference catalogs
Design approval records
Procedures that omit prerequisites, outcomes, or consequential warnings

sample_tasks.instruction: Using a completed documentation plan, write a short procedure with a goal, one prerequisite, ordered actions, and an observable completion state.

For a small software service, create a coordinated support set containing an onboarding tutorial, a focused operational how-to, a conceptual explanation of an important behavior, and a symptom-driven troubleshooting guide with consistent terminology and cross-references.

sections.name: How-To Guides
sections.outcome: Write concise procedures that help a prepared reader accomplish a specific technical goal safely and verify the result.
excludes: Broad conceptual teaching
Exhaustive parameter reference
Open-ended diagnosis before a cause is known

sample_tasks.instruction: For a defined reader and a three-action task, write the ordered actions and one observable completion check.

Write a focused guide for configuring and running a command-line data export, including prerequisites, exact action order, conditional branches, a consequential warning, and checks that confirm the intended file was produced.

sections.name: Tutorials
sections.outcome: Guide a learner through a complete, achievable experience that builds transferable understanding through sequenced practice and checkpoints.
excludes: Unexplained command sequences
Comprehensive reference coverage
Troubleshooting organized primarily by failure symptom

sample_tasks.instruction: Take a mastered short procedure and add a learning goal, one prerequisite, and one checkpoint that reveals why a key action matters.

Create a first-use tutorial in which the defined learner builds, runs, inspects, and modifies a small application, with a coherent example, progressive explanations, checkpoints, and a final exercise that transfers the learned pattern.

sections.name: Technical Explanations
sections.outcome: Explain technical behavior, distinctions, and tradeoffs so a defined reader can reason about when and why to use an approach.
excludes: Procedures whose main purpose is task completion
Reference entries organized by symbols or fields
Unsupported universal performance claims

sample_tasks.instruction: Using verified behavior and a reader profile, explain one technical distinction and one practical consequence in a short paragraph.

Explain several approaches to iterating over a mutable collection, comparing semantics, readability, compatibility, and measured performance, then give a qualified recommendation for the stated operating context.

sections.name: Troubleshooting Guides
sections.outcome: Lead readers from an observable symptom through discriminating checks to supported causes, corrective actions, and confirmation of recovery.
excludes: Lists of generic fixes with no diagnostic path
Implementation tutorials for systems that are working normally
Speculative causes presented as confirmed

sample_tasks.instruction: Given a known symptom and two supported causes, write one check that distinguishes the causes and one corrective action for each result.

Create a troubleshooting guide for intermittent stale responses in a client-server application, covering reproduction, request lifecycle checks, cache and response-order tests, cause-specific client or server remedies, recovery verification, and escalation evidence.

sections.name: Specifications and Design Documents
sections.outcome: Document what a system must accomplish, evaluate how it could be built, and preserve the rationale and consequences of the selected design.
excludes: Specifications of an already completed product as lookup reference
Implementation tutorials
Project status reporting without design content

sample_tasks.instruction: Using a completed audience, evidence, and structure plan, express one stated need as a measurable design objective and identify one constraint.

For a proposed event-processing service, produce a coherent design packet containing testable requirements, an option-based design proposal, and a decision record that preserves the chosen architecture, rejected alternatives, rationale, and consequences.

sections.name: Technical Requirements
sections.outcome: Convert stakeholder and operational needs into atomic, unambiguous, feasible, and verifiable requirements.
excludes: Implementation choices not required by a stated constraint
Current-product feature catalogs
Vague aspirations without measurable conditions

sample_tasks.instruction: Convert one supported stakeholder need into a single requirement with a measurable success condition.

Write a requirements section for a shared capture service, covering functional behavior, latency, reliability, security, compatibility, and operational constraints, with atomic statements and verifiable acceptance criteria tied to the supplied needs.

sections.name: Design Proposals
sections.outcome: Present a technical problem, constraints, candidate designs, tradeoffs, recommendation, and implementation consequences clearly enough for informed review.
excludes: Decisions stated without alternatives or rationale
Detailed implementation manuals
Requirements lists with no design response

sample_tasks.instruction: Given one testable requirement and two viable approaches, compare the approaches on one relevant tradeoff and recommend one.

Using a structured set of requirements, write a design proposal for changing a data-ingestion path, including context, goals and non-goals, candidate architectures, tradeoffs, the recommended design, failure handling, migration, observability, and unresolved questions.

sections.name: Architecture Decision Records
sections.outcome: Preserve a settled technical decision with enough context, alternatives, rationale, status, and consequences for later maintainers to understand and revisit it.
excludes: Open proposals with no decision
Meeting transcripts
Restating implementation details without rationale

sample_tasks.instruction: From a completed comparison of two designs, record the chosen option, the deciding reason, and one consequence.

Convert a reviewed design proposal into an architecture decision record that summarizes the governing requirements, records the chosen design and rejected alternatives, explains the tradeoffs, states operational consequences, and defines when the decision should be reconsidered.

sections.name: Documentation Quality and Maintenance
sections.outcome: Deliver documentation that conforms to explicit constraints, is clear and internally consistent, and remains accurate as the documented system changes.
excludes: Changing system behavior to match incorrect documentation
Cosmetic editing that preserves a known factual error
Unrequested expansion of document scope

sample_tasks.instruction: Apply a supplied heading pattern, terminology rule, and output format to one short planned technical passage without changing its meaning.

Using the audience, evidence, and structure plan for a small documentation set, enforce its template and delivery rules, revise unclear and inconsistent passages, incorporate a product change, repair affected cross-references, and record the maintenance impact.

sections.name: Format and Delivery Compliance
sections.outcome: Render technical content under exact structural, lexical, serialization, and delivery requirements without losing required meaning.
excludes: Choosing arbitrary style rules
Schema-valid data modeling as the central task
Sacrificing technical correctness to satisfy presentation constraints

sample_tasks.instruction: Reformat a short technical note to use a required title, exactly two sections, and a specified final line while preserving every factual claim.

Produce a complete technical response under simultaneous requirements for section count, section ordering, prescribed opening and closing text, restricted terminology, code-block placement, and a specified plain-text delivery format; audit the result against each requirement.

sections.name: Technical Revision
sections.outcome: Revise technical prose and structure to improve correctness, clarity, concision, consistency, and task usability for the intended reader.
includes: Removal of unsupported or redundant content
excludes: Pure proofreading limited to spelling
Adding facts absent from the evidence
Rewriting to a different document type without need

sample_tasks.instruction: Revise one ambiguous technical sentence so the defined reader can identify the actor, action, condition, and result without changing the supported claim.

Revise a short developer guide for its defined audience by correcting unsupported claims, resolving inconsistent terminology, removing redundancy, clarifying conditions and warnings, and reorganizing the material around the reader's task while preserving all supported technical meaning.

sections.name: Documentation Maintenance
sections.outcome: Update a versioned documentation set after system changes while preserving consistency, traceability, working navigation, and an accurate account of compatibility impact.
excludes: Unrelated cleanup across unchanged pages
Backward-compatibility promises unsupported by the product
Replacing historical decisions with current conclusions

sample_tasks.instruction: Given one changed option name, revise the affected sentence for clarity and update its single incoming cross-reference.

Given an old documentation set, current behavior, and a release change list, first revise the affected material for accuracy and clarity, then update version and compatibility statements, migration guidance, examples, navigation, cross-references, and the documentation change record without altering unaffected content.
